transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um… I guess work has been kind of hard lately. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but people got worried.

I wait tables, and during service I’ve been sort of… freezing up. Like I’ll be in the middle of doing something and just stop. Or I’ll do things in the wrong order. One time I was standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers instead of closing out checks like I was supposed to.

It scared people, I think. I’m sorry, I know that probably sounds strange.
Have you gone through any particularly stressful or upsetting events recently, either at work or in your personal life?

I don’t think so… not anything big, at least. Work is always stressful, but that’s normal, right? I mean, restaurants get busy and people get irritated, but I can usually handle that.

Personally… I’m not sure. Nothing happened that I’d point to and say, “that’s what caused it.” I kind of wish there was something obvious to explain it, honestly.
Has anything like this ever happened to you before, where you felt like you were freezing up or couldn’t think clearly?

Not really before this, not in a way people noticed. I mean, I’ve had normal moments where I’m tired or overwhelmed, sure, but this was different.

The main thing was at work, during service. I’d kind of stop in the middle of what I was doing, or do things in the wrong order. Like that time by the soda station… I had the cash drawer key in my hand, and instead of closing checks, I was just repeating table numbers. I know that sounds bad. I wasn’t trying to be difficult or anything.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

I wouldn’t say hopeless exactly… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it. But I guess I haven’t really been doing the things I used to do much.

Like, I used to go for walks on the beach, bake sometimes, do a little gardening, write in my journal… and lately I just don’t really start any of it. My husband will try to talk with me, and I mostly just sit there. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude. It just feels like I can’t get myself to care enough or get going, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way — not getting started on things, not enjoying your usual activities, and having trouble during work?

I think… it’s been longer than I wanted to admit. Maybe about a year and a couple months? It kind of started after I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities.

At first I told myself it was just adjusting to more responsibility, and maybe that’s still part of it, I don’t know. But looking back, that’s around when I started feeling like I wasn’t really myself and things got harder to start or keep straight. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge lately, even when there isn’t anything specific you can point to as the cause?

I don’t think so… not unusually, anyway. I mean, I get nervous about work sometimes, or about messing things up, but I can usually point to a reason.

I wouldn’t say I’m just on edge for no reason all the time. Unless I’m not noticing it? I’m trying to answer that right.
Have you noticed feeling more tired than usual or lacking energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

I’m not sure… I mean, I do get tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. Work can be tiring, so I sort of blame it on that.

On days I’m not doing much, I guess I don’t always feel very energetic, but I haven’t really been tracking it. I don’t want to say yes if it’s just me being lazy or something. Is that helpful, or do you mean like exhausted all the time?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think I’ve had a big change like that. My appetite is maybe a little uneven with my shifts, but I haven’t noticed eating way less or losing weight without trying.

I mean, my clothes seem about the same. I can keep an eye on it if that’s important?
On days when you haven’t been doing much, do you find that you still feel fatigued or lack energy, even without physical exertion?

I don’t know if I’d call it fatigued exactly. Like, if I’m just home and not doing much, I can still feel kind of low-energy, but I usually tell myself it’s just from work or not sleeping perfectly or… I don’t know.

It’s not like I can’t get up or anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe a little sometimes, but I’m not sure if that counts?
When you’re not at work, do you still find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, like walking on the beach, baking, or gardening?

A little, I guess… not as much as I used to. I don’t really go for beach walks much anymore, or bake, or garden. Even journaling, I kind of just… don’t do it.

It’s not that I hate those things now. I just can’t seem to get started, or I don’t feel much pull toward them. And when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there sometimes. I know that probably sounds bad — I’m not trying to be cold. It just feels like I can’t quite make myself care or respond the way I should. Does that make sense?
Do you find that you feel down or sad most of the day, even when there isn't anything specific going on to explain it?

I’m not sure I’d say “sad most of the day,” exactly. I mean, I have moments where I feel kind of low or flat, but there isn’t always a reason I can point to.

I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more like… some days I’m just not very up, if that makes sense. But I can still get through things. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions, even about small things?

Um… yeah, maybe a bit. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I can usually manage, but at work people got worried because I’d kind of freeze up in the middle of service.

Like, I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I’d just be repeating table numbers to myself. Or I’d do things out of order and then not really know what I was supposed to do next. It was embarrassing. I kept trying to play it off like I was just busy or distracted, but… I guess it did look odd. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find that your low or flat mood tends to happen most days, even when nothing specific is going on?

Yeah… I think it probably is most days, if I’m being honest. Not like I’m crying or anything, so I don’t know if “low mood” is exactly the right word. It’s more flat, or just… hard to get interested.

Like I don’t really go walk on the beach, or bake, or garden, or write in my journal much anymore. And when my husband tries to talk with me, sometimes I mostly just sit there. I feel bad saying that — I’m not trying to be dismissive. It just feels like I can’t quite get myself to care or start things the way I used to.

Is that answering what you mean?
Do you find that your low or flat mood happens on most days, even when there’s nothing specific going on to explain it?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s kind of there most days — more like flat than sad.

I’ve noticed I don’t really do the things I used to, like going for walks on the beach, or baking, or gardening, or writing in my journal. And when my husband tries to talk to me, sometimes I mostly just sit there. It’s not that I don’t care about him… I just feel like I can’t get myself to care or start anything, if that makes sense. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like walking on the beach, baking, gardening, or writing in your journal?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want it to sound like I’ve just given up on everything, but I don’t really go for beach walks anymore, or bake, or garden, or write in my journal much.

Those used to feel like easy things, or good things, and now they just feel like… too much effort, or like I can’t get myself to start. And when my husband tries to talk with me, sometimes I mostly just sit there. I feel bad about that. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore him. I just don’t seem to feel much interest, I guess. Is that what you mean?
